response:
I read the fixture source for the findings I was going to move up or down, so the departures from the tool's ranking below are verified, not vibes.

## How I'm reading the two axes

`severity` and `scores.agent_risk` are near-orthogonal in this scan, and neither alone gives a merge decision:

- `large_function` is severity **0.90** / agent_risk **0.13**; `direct_date` is severity **0.60** / agent_risk **0.45**. Sorting on either column alone produces a wrong triage.
- **`blast_radius` is 0 on all 39 findings** and `blast_radius_direct_importers` is 0 everywhere — this repo has almost no internal import graph. `recency` is also 0 across the board despite `ranking.recency_enabled: true` (empty baseline, no history). Both inputs are dead, so agent_risk is compressed into 0.04–0.45. **Treat agent_risk as a relative ordering within this scan, not an absolute threshold.** Nothing here scoring 0.45 would score 0.45 in a repo with real fan-in.
- Baseline is empty, so "new vs. pre-existing" cannot filter anything. All 39 are new.

So: severity answers *how wrong is it*, agent_risk answers *how likely is the next agent to make it worse*, and I block only where a third thing is true — it is cheap to fix **and** it is wrong on every machine, or it silently lies.

## Block merge — 8 findings

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | why block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00018 | Localhost-on-Disk | 0.60 | 0.31 | `SCHEMA_PATH = "/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json"`. `loadPlanSchema()` guards with `existsSync` and **returns `null`** — so it doesn't crash, it silently returns no schema on every machine but one. Silent-null beats a crash for badness. Also commits a developer's username. `effort: quick`. |
| 00017 | Dev-Server URL | 0.60 | 0.31 | `adminUrl()` returns `http://localhost:3000/admin` unconditionally. Any environment that renders an admin link ships a dead one. `effort: quick`. |
| 00032 | Catch and Release | 0.35 | **0.16** | **Escalated well above its score.** Verified at `src/billing.ts:245`: the catch is bare (`catch {`), then lines 249–250 write `metadata.emailAttempts` and `emailLatencyMs` onto the returned invoice. A failed send is recorded on a money document as a completed attempt. The "retry loop" also has no backoff and `break`s on success, so `attempts` is always 1. crimes ranks this 32/39; the evidence line "no sensitive operation evidenced" is what deflates it, and it's wrong here — the operation is invoice email. |
| 00027 + 00030 | Test That Proves Nothing | 0.45 / 0.25 | 0.28 / 0.24 | **Escalated.** The detector says "no assertions" and "weak matchers". The real fact is worse: `src/billing.test.ts` imports only `vitest` — it never imports `billing.ts`. `createInvoice()` and `renderEnterprisePlan()` are local stubs defined at the bottom of the test file returning `{ id: "invoice_123" }`. The suite passes against nothing. A 310-line billing engine lands with **zero** coverage while appearing covered. |
| 00005 + 00021 | Half-UTC, Half-Local + Date String Sewing | 0.80 / 0.30 | 0.39 / 0.29 | Same expression, `src/date.ts:41`. `dateLabel()` returns `d.getUTCFullYear() + "-" + d.getMonth() + "-" + d.getDate()` — a UTC year concatenated to a **local, 0-indexed** month and a local day. In January in a UTC+ zone this is wrong in the year, the month *and* the day simultaneously. Highest-severity finding that is also plainly, deterministically incorrect output. Small fix. (00021 is not a separate task — fixing 00005 dissolves it.) |
| 00033 | God Function | 0.90 | **0.13** | `generateInvoice` at 204 lines. I would normally warn on length alone — I block on the **conjunction**: this one body contains the swallowed error (00032), 5 of the 7 clock reads (00009), the commented-out corpse (00028), and a copy of the tax table that `tax()` at line 256 duplicates. None of it is tested (see above). The 0.13 agent_risk is an artefact of zero blast radius; the in-file coupling is the whole problem. |

## Warn — 24 findings

Land the PR with these tracked; none is a correctness emergency, several are cheap.

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00011 | Contract Split-Brain `User` | 0.90 | 0.37 | **De-escalated from its high severity.** Verified: *neither* declaration is exported, and neither file imports the other — `src/api/state.ts:4` and `src/billing.ts:4` are both file-local. `blast_radius: 0` is accurate. `state.ts` self-documents as "fixture material — do not import". The drift is inert today; the residual risk is an agent grepping `interface User` and getting two answers. Warn, not block. |
| 00012 | Contract Split-Brain `Invoice` | 0.96 | 0.37 | Same structural de-escalation — **but** this is the highest-severity finding in the scan for a reason: the `billing.ts` version carries `subtotalCents`/`taxCents`/`discountCents`/`currency`/`userId`, the `state.ts` version has `{id, totalCents}`. If either is ever exported, money fields vanish on one side. Track as the first thing to fix if these types go public. |
| 00003 | Missing Agent Context | 0.60 | 0.43 | #3 by agent_risk and correctly so — this PR adds an entire repo with no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. `effort: small`. Borderline block; warn only because it degrades future changes, not this one. |
| 00001 | Temporal Recklessness (date.ts) | 0.60 | **0.45** | Top of the scan by agent_risk. Evidence distinguishes well: 1 of 6 reads *decides a branch* (`isExpired`, L4), 5 only render. The branching one is the untestable one. |
| 00009 | Temporal Recklessness (billing.ts) | 0.60 | 0.38 | 7 reads, evidence says **none decide a branch** — output-only. Genuinely lower risk than 00001 despite the larger count; good scoring. |
| 00010 | Timezone Roulette | 0.60 | 0.38 | `new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00")` (local) next to `new Date("2026-12-20")` (UTC midnight) in the same file. The promo window is off by up to a day, direction depending on host zone. **Promote to block if promo windows gate revenue** — one character each to fix. |
| 00016 | DST-Naive Day Math | 0.60 | 0.33 | `nowMs + 86400000`. Wrong twice a year. `effort: medium` is the only thing keeping it out of the block list. |
| 00022 | Host-Locale Drift | 0.30 | 0.29 | `due.toLocaleDateString()` — same date.ts cluster; fix with 00005/00016 in one pass. |
| 00014 | False Identity | 0.55 | 0.35 | `calculateRefundPreview` awaits `saveRefundAudit` **and** `sendRefundEmail`, then returns `invoice.totalCents`. A "preview" that emails the customer. Rename is `effort: small` and removes a real footgun. |
| 00015 | Logic in the Alibi | 0.50 | 0.35 | The comment at L39 — "Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves" — sits directly above `calculateRefundPreview`, which enforces **none** of it. An authorization rule exists only as prose. Warn now, block if refunds become reachable. |
| 00028 | Commented-Out Corpse | 0.45 | 0.27 | See governance note below — this one has a lapsed decision attached. |
| 00024–00026 | Orphaned Destination ×3 | 0.40 | 0.29 | `/account/subscription`, `/team`, `/workspace/members` — three unreachable route trees in one PR. Read together with 00019 this isn't three orphans, it's one design problem (below). |
| 00019 | Concept Alias Drift | 0.55 | 0.31 | The `tenant` group appears as account / organisation / team / workspace across 5 files. **The three orphaned routes are the three aliases.** The PR ships three parallel route trees for one concept and wires up none of them. Decide the canonical term before any of these routes goes live; otherwise the next agent adds a fourth. |
| 00006 | Duplicated Navigation Source | 0.60 | 0.39 | `/settings/billing` is "Plans" in `registry.ts`, "Billing" in `sidebar.ts`. |
| 00007 | Route Metadata Drift | 0.60 | 0.39 | Same destination named 4 ways (path/`PricingPage`/`metadata.title: Plans`/`<title>: Subscription`). Same fix as 00006 — one source of truth resolves both. |
| 00004 | String Sprinkles | 0.50 | 0.43 | `"enterprise"` in 4 files across api/billing/jobs/ui. Note the suggested action carries `risk: medium` — centralising blind can merge intentionally-divergent policy. Confirm shared semantics first. |
| 00031 | Phantom Accomplice | 0.25 | 0.24 | `vitest` imported, declared nowhere — `package.json` has **no dependencies block at all**. A clean install cannot run the test suite. Confidence is discounted to 0.56 because only test files are affected; that discount is fair, the fix is still one line. |
| 00034 | Unfinished Business (todo.ts) | 0.40 | 0.10 | 424 markers/1k LOC — the file is more TODO than code, and it self-describes as an in-memory store that "loses data on restart". That's a declared-incomplete persistence layer, which is a scope question for the PR author, not a comment-hygiene issue. |
| 00020 | Temporal Recklessness (state.ts) | 0.35 | 0.29 | Single branching read in the fixture-marked file. |
| 00002 | Return Shape Roulette | 0.30 | 0.44 | **0% key overlap** across 3 return shapes from `resolvePaymentResult` — `{code,message,ok}` vs `{permanent,url}`. Low severity, high relative agent_risk, and the high agent_risk is the correct read: callers cannot narrow this. |
| 00029 | Docs-Code Drift | 0.35 | 0.25 | `docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md` (missing). Weighted up slightly by 00003: with no AGENTS.md, docs are the *only* agent guidance, so a dead link in them costs more than usual. |
| 00036 | God File | 0.60 | 0.07 | 310 lines vs a 300 threshold — 1.0×, i.e. barely over. Redundant with 00033; splitting the god function dissolves this. Don't track it separately. |

## Ignore — 7 findings

| id | charge | sev | agent_risk | why ignore |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00035 | SVG With Embedded Raster | **0.75** | **0.08** | The clearest severity/risk divergence in the scan. A **592-byte** SVG with two embedded rasters — the severity ladder is about page weight, and at 592 bytes there is no page weight. High severity, zero consequence. |
| 00037 | Oversized Raster | 0.40 | 0.05 | 254 KB, the bottom rung of a 200/500/1000 KB ladder. Asset budget item, not a merge gate. |
| 00038 | Icon-Sized Raster | 0.35 | 0.05 | 32×32 PNG. Design-tooling preference. |
| 00039 | Unfinished Business (billing.ts) | 0.20 | 0.04 | 4 markers at 12.9/1k against a threshold of 10 — 1.3× over. Noise, and the markers point at things already tracked as 00032/00033. |
| 00023 | Plural Mismatch | 0.30 | 0.29 | In the file that declares itself non-importable fixture material, and the evidence self-limits: "v1 detector — type aliases and generic types are silently skipped." |
| 00013 | Negative Flag Maze | 0.25 | 0.37 | `!disableBilling && !skipRetry` — two negations in one condition is still readable. Revisit if a third flag joins. |
| 00008 | Option Bag Junk Drawer | 0.30 | 0.39 | `src/petty.ts` has an actual `interface CheckoutOptions` at line 1; the shape isn't as implicit as the finding assumes. Contained to one function. |

## Governance: one lapsed decision, not a fixed one

`coverage.warnings` reports a **superseded** suppression, and it matters more than it looks. `.crimes/suppressions.json` pins `commented_out_code::src/billing.ts::` with the reason *"kept in comments for one more release; will be deleted in v0.3."* The current finding's fingerprint is `commented_out_code::src/billing.ts::::42a4bbb39f1f` — the discriminator joined the fingerprint at schema 0.8.0, so **00028 is visible again with nothing silencing it**. Nobody re-approved it; the pin just stopped matching.

Don't re-pin by hand. Run `crimes migrate-pins --format json`, review the destination, then either apply it or — since the reason says v3 was the deadline and the snippet is still there — just delete the five commented lines and drop the suppression. Do not silently renew it.

## Beyond the scan

Two things the detectors don't claim but a reviewer should:

- `package.json` declares `"bin": {"messy": "src/billing.ts"}` — a TypeScript file as an executable entry point, with no build step and no dependencies. That bin cannot run. This is the same `package.json` that 00031 flags and that 00003 cites as evidence ("declares bin(s): messy — agents have no way to discover commands").
- `tax()` at `src/billing.ts:256` duplicates the country/rate table that lives inside `generateInvoice`. No detector fired on it — the file's own comment does. A rate change has to land in two places, and nothing in the build connects them. Worth a warn-level ticket alongside 00033.

**One caveat on all of the above:** `coverage.warnings` also notes 1 file was never read (`.crimes/suppressions.json`, matched by `exclude` — benign here). Findings in excluded files are absent, not zero, and a clean exit from `crimes scan` doesn't establish that the rest is safe.
